item.title: Computer Safety Tips
item.description:
Computer security protects computer systems and information from theft and unauthorized access. Use the following practices to reduce common risks.

Do

  • Download applications and software only from trusted sources.
  • Keep the operating system, applications, and antivirus software updated.
  • Back up important data, files, and documents at regular intervals.
  • Lock the computer screen whenever it is not in use.
  • Keep the computer firewall enabled.
  • Use an account with limited privileges where possible.
  • Use genuine and licensed software.
  • Scan files downloaded from websites, email, or USB devices.
  • Uninstall programs that are no longer needed.
  • Use Task Manager to identify unwanted programs running on the system.
  • Allow server access through multi-factor authentication.
  • Disable Remote Desktop and network file sharing when they are not needed.
  • Enable automatic operating system updates.

Do not

  • Install or use pirated software, which may contain malware.
  • Use weak or easily guessed passwords.
  • Click untrusted or unexpected pop-up advertisements and programs.
  • Dispose of a computer or hard drive without securely deleting and wiping its data.

item.title: USB Device Security
item.description:
USB devices are convenient for transferring data, but their portability can introduce data theft, data leakage, and malware risks. Examples include flash drives, portable hard drives, memory cards, cameras, mobile phones, and USB keyboards or mice.

Safe practices

  • Scan every USB device with antivirus or endpoint protection before using it.
  • Disable Autorun and Autoplay on computers when using USB devices.
  • Avoid connecting unknown or untrusted USB devices.
  • Disable or remove USB devices when they are not needed.

item.title: Password Security Management
item.description:
Passwords restrict access to information and systems to authorized users. Strong, unique passwords help defend against dictionary attacks, brute-force attacks, and password-capturing tools such as keyloggers.

Do

  • Use a different strong password for every account.
  • Use a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
  • Change a password immediately if it has been shared or revealed.
  • Change passwords at regular intervals when required by the service or policy.
  • Use passwords of at least thirteen characters where supported.

Do not

  • Include birth dates, names, identity details, addresses, or phone numbers.
  • Use names of family members, pets, friends, colleagues, or fictional characters.
  • Use a password that is short or easy to guess.
  • Access banking or other sensitive services from public computers.
  • Share passwords or one-time passwords through email, chat, or other electronic communication.
  • Reveal passwords in questionnaires or security forms.
  • Save passwords in a browser on banking or other sensitive sites.
  • Write passwords down where they can be found, such as on a note next to the computer.
  • Use biometrics at untrusted terminals or locations.

Password Managers and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Password Managers

Use a reputable password manager (built-in options from major browsers/OS or dedicated tools) to generate and store unique, long passwords (ideally 15+ characters or passphrases) for every account.

item.title: General Internet Safety Precautions
item.description:
Unsafe internet use can expose people and organizations to phishing, viruses, trojans, worms, ransomware, business email compromise, and financial loss.

Do

  • Be cautious when clicking links or downloading from suspicious URLs.
  • Clear browser history after confidential activities or transactions.
  • Configure appropriate security and privacy settings for cloud storage.
  • Verify the authenticity and identity of social media profiles before corresponding with them.
  • Use services that request location information judiciously.
  • Avoid posting photos with GPS coordinates.
  • Check advertisements and sponsored content on search results and websites.
  • Verify the source and authenticity of content before sharing it.

Do not

  • Use public computers or public Wi-Fi for online shopping, internet banking, UPI, or other financial transactions.
  • Enter email addresses, phone numbers, or payment-card details on untrusted and unsecured websites.
  • Trust or share unverified content from social media, messaging apps, email, text messages, or phone calls.
  • Respond to messages asking for passwords or other sensitive information without verifying the source.

item.title: Financial Transactions - Safe Practices
item.description:
Internet banking, UPI, cards, and mobile banking make payments convenient, but a security lapse can cause financial loss.

UPI and payment safety

  • Keep the UPI PIN secret and never share it.
  • Remember that a UPI PIN is not required to receive money.
  • Protect the device and payment application with a strong passcode.
  • Verify the payee name and QR code before confirming a payment.

Card safety

  • Treat the card number, expiry date, CVV, and OTP as confidential.
  • Never share card details or OTPs with anyone.
  • Use cards only after checking the authenticity of the point-of-sale terminal, ATM, or website.
  • Manage card limits through mobile banking for additional protection.

Internet and mobile banking

  • Use genuine and licensed operating systems for banking transactions.
  • Verify banking URLs received by SMS or email before entering credentials.
  • Use a strong banking password that is different from passwords for email, shopping, and other accounts.
  • Avoid public computers and insecure internet connections for banking.

item.title: Social Media Platforms - Safety Tips
item.description:
Use social media carefully to protect personal information, location details, and the authenticity of shared content.

Do

  • Choose privacy settings carefully before sharing content.
  • Be cautious when revealing location information online.
  • Verify friend requests before accepting them.
  • Verify content before forwarding or sharing it.
  • Enable multi-factor authentication on social media accounts.

Do not

  • Use a social media account without multi-factor authentication.
  • Log in to social media accounts from untrusted systems.
  • Share personal or location information without considering who can access it.

item.title: Mobile Phone Safety
item.description:
Mobile phones hold personal and organizational data. Poor security can lead to data theft, financial loss, unauthorized access, and malware infection.

Do

  • Be cautious when using public Wi-Fi because information shared over it may be misused.
  • Review the default privacy settings of the phone, applications, and social media accounts.
  • Check an application’s reputation, authenticity, privacy policy, and permissions before installing it.
  • Download applications from genuine sources.
  • Turn off or remove unnecessary applications.
  • Register for the Do Not Disturb service with the telecom operator.
  • Use parental controls when handing a phone to a child or minor.
  • Encrypt the device and SD card to protect confidential data.
  • Protect the device with a strong PIN, password, or biometrics and enable auto-lock.
  • Back up contacts, photos, and other important data regularly.

Do not

  • Reply to or click links sent by strangers through SMS, email, or chat.
  • Store classified or sensitive data, including text, video, or photographs, unnecessarily on the device.
  • Log in to financial or other sensitive accounts over public wireless networks.

item.title: Malware Protection
item.description:
Malware is malicious software designed to perform unauthorized or destructive tasks without the user’s knowledge. It can lock files, steal sensitive information, provide unauthorized remote access, monitor activity, consume resources, or corrupt files.

Common types include spyware, viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, and botnets.

Protection practices

  • Keep the operating system and all applications up to date.
  • Apply security patches to address vulnerabilities.
  • Do not click untrusted URL links.
  • Use an up-to-date anti-malware solution.
  • Scan files regularly and scan USB devices before use.
  • Disable USB devices when they are not needed.
  • Use licensed operating systems and application software.

item.title: Email Security Practices
item.description:
Email messages can contain links that attempt to steal personal, financial, or organizational information.

Safe practices

  • Do not open or reply to links in emails that offer luring or unexpected benefits.
  • Verify the sender before accessing a spam or suspicious email.
  • Treat hyperlinks, web links, and URLs in email bodies with caution.
  • Do not provide personal or financial details in response to an unverified email.
  • Verify the authenticity of an email through a trusted channel before taking action.
